transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well... I guess what scared me enough to actually come in today is my thoughts lately. I just keep thinking that it would be a relief if I went to sleep and just didn't wake up. I haven't tried to hurt myself or anything like that. But just having those kinds of thoughts... it frightened me, so I figured I needed to talk to somebody.
Have you thought about how you might kill yourself?

No, I haven't. Like I was just saying, I don't have a plan and I haven't tried to hurt myself. It's really just... I just keep thinking it would be such a relief if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. I haven't thought about actually doing anything to make that happen, but just having those kinds of thoughts is what scared me enough to come in today.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or irritable and you felt much more energetic than usual?

No, I can't say I've ever felt like that. I've never had a time where I felt unusually high or full of energy, or anything like that. I'm usually just... well, tired, mostly. But no, nothing like what you're describing.
Did these thoughts begin after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
Well, yes, I suppose it did. This has all been going on for about four months now... right around the time my aunt came to live with us.
During this period, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. I used to really look forward to doing my watercolors, going to dance class, and walking with the ladies. But lately... well, I just leave my painting things sitting there. I just can't seem to make myself care about doing any of it anymore.
During these past four months, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day on most days?

Yes, I have. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy sadness right here in my chest. It just... it feels like I've already failed the day before it even starts. It's just a very down, hopeless kind of feeling that sticks with me most of the day.
How has your sleep been during these past four months?
Well, honestly... I haven't really noticed any big changes with my sleep. I guess I sleep about the same as I always have. I haven't really paid too much attention to it, to be honest.
During these past four months, how has your energy been compared with usual?

It's just been really low. Even after a full night in bed, my body just feels... worn out. It's like doing the simplest things, like carrying a basket of laundry or just making breakfast, takes way more out of me than it should. I just don't have the energy I used to.
During these past four months, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?
No, I wouldn't say so. My mind still seems clear enough. I can focus on things fine, and... well, making decisions hasn't really been a problem for me. I haven't noticed any changes with that.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite during these past four months?
No, my appetite has been pretty normal. I'm eating about the same amount I usually do. I haven't noticed any changes there.
During these past four months, have you been feeling excessively guilty or worthless?

Well, yes, actually. I take care of my aunt, and... sometimes I just get so tired, or I get annoyed with her. And when that happens, I just start thinking that I'm a bad woman. I feel like I'm bringing shame on my family because I should be more grateful, you know? It just makes me feel awful about myself.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your ability to manage your usual daily activities and responsibilities?

Well, they've interfered a fair amount, I suppose. I've stopped going to my dance class and my walking group. I just don't have the energy for it. And I haven't been going to my shifts at the food pantry either. I just... I get stuck, and I fall behind on things. My husband has had to take over doing more of the errands because I just can't seem to get them done like I used to.
